verses.text: Ahab had seventy sons living in Samaria. So Jehu wrote letters and sent them to Samaria, to the officials of Jezreel, to the leaders, and to the men who were raising Ahab's sons. He wrote,
"Your master's sons are with you, and you have chariots and horses, a walled city, and weapons. So as soon as this letter reaches you,
choose the best and most able of your master's sons. Put him on his father's throne, and fight for your master's family."
But they were terrified. They said, "Two kings could not stand against him. How can we?"

So the man in charge of the palace, the governor of the city, the leaders, and the men raising the sons sent this message to Jehu: "We are your servants, and we will do anything you tell us. We will not make anyone king. Do whatever you think is best."

Then Jehu wrote them a second letter. He said, "If you are on my side and will obey me, bring the heads of your master's sons to me in Jezreel by this time tomorrow." The seventy sons of the king were being raised by the leading men of the city.
When the letter arrived, these men took the seventy sons of the king and killed them all. They put their heads in baskets and sent them to Jehu at Jezreel.
A messenger came and told Jehu, "They have brought the heads of the king's sons." Jehu said, "Put them in two piles at the entrance of the city gate until morning."
The next morning Jehu went out, stood in front of all the people, and said, "You are not to blame. It is true that I plotted against my master and killed him. But who killed all these?
Know this: not one word the LORD spoke against Ahab's family will fail to come true. The LORD has done what he said through his servant Elijah."
So Jehu killed everyone in Jezreel who was left from Ahab's family, along with all his important officials, his close friends, and his priests. He left no one alive.
Then Jehu set out for Samaria. On the way, at Beth Eked, where the shepherds sheared their sheep,
he met some relatives of Ahaziah king of Judah. He asked, "Who are you?" They answered, "We are relatives of Ahaziah. We have come down to visit the king's sons and the queen mother's sons."
Jehu ordered, "Take them alive!" So they took them alive and then killed them at the well of Beth Eked, forty-two men. He did not leave any of them alive.

When Jehu left there, he met Jehonadab son of Rechab, who was coming to meet him. Jehu greeted him and asked, "Are you as loyal to me as I am to you?" Jehonadab answered, "I am." Jehu said, "If you are, give me your hand." So he gave him his hand, and Jehu helped him up into the chariot.
Jehu said, "Come with me and see how zealous I am for the LORD." So Jehonadab rode along with him in his chariot.
When Jehu arrived in Samaria, he killed everyone in Samaria who was left from Ahab's family. He wiped them out, just as the LORD had told Elijah.
Then Jehu gathered all the people together and said, "Ahab served Baal a little. Jehu will serve him a lot.

Now call together all the prophets of Baal, all his worshippers, and all his priests. Make sure no one is missing, because I am going to offer a great sacrifice to Baal. Anyone who does not come will be put to death." But Jehu was tricking them, so he could destroy the worshippers of Baal.
Jehu said, "Call a holy gathering to honour Baal." So they announced it.
Jehu sent word through all Israel, and all the worshippers of Baal came. Not one of them stayed away. They crowded into the temple of Baal until it was full from one end to the other.
Jehu told the man in charge of the robes, "Bring out robes for all the worshippers of Baal." So he brought robes out for them.

Then Jehu and Jehonadab son of Rechab went into the temple of Baal. Jehu said to the worshippers of Baal, "Look around and make sure there are no servants of the LORD here with you, only worshippers of Baal."

So they went in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Jehu had posted eighty men outside. He had warned them, "If anyone lets even one of the people I hand over to you escape, he will pay with his own life."

As soon as Jehu finished offering the burnt offering, he ordered the guards and officers, "Go in and kill them! Do not let anyone get away." So they killed them with their swords. The guards and officers threw the bodies out and then went into the inner room of Baal's temple.
They brought out the sacred stone pillars from the temple of Baal and burned them.
They smashed the sacred stone of Baal and tore down the temple of Baal. They turned it into a public toilet, and it is still one today.
So Jehu wiped out the worship of Baal in Israel.
But Jehu did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had made Israel sin. He kept the gold calves at Bethel and Dan.

The LORD said to Jehu, "You have done well by doing what is right in my eyes. You have done to Ahab's family everything I wanted done. So your descendants will sit on the throne of Israel for four generations."
But Jehu was not careful to obey the law of the LORD, the God of Israel, with all his heart. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam, who had made Israel sin.
In those days the LORD began to make Israel smaller. Hazael defeated the Israelites all along their borders.

He conquered the land east of the Jordan River, all the land of Gilead, where the tribes of Gad, Reuben, and Manasseh lived. He took it from Aroer by the Arnon Valley all the way through Gilead and Bashan.
The rest of what Jehu did, all his deeds and all his power, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Israel.
Jehu died and was buried in Samaria. His son Jehoahaz became king after him.
Jehu ruled over Israel in Samaria for twenty-eight years.
